title.en: Portage Lake: Memories of an Ojibwe Childhood

div.title: Portage Lake: Memories of an Ojibwe Childhood
div.speaker: Maude Kegg

chapter.eng_title: When I Was a Little Girl

paragraph.text_eng: Long ago, when I was a little girl, my grandmother's husband died. Then there was only my uncle and his wife, and there were two women, young women. That's just how many of us there were, along with one aunt of mine. That's just how many of us there were.

sentence.sent_text: Mewinzha gii-ikwezensiwiyaan, gaa-nibonid iniw onaabeman a'aw nookomis.
Miish eta go inzhishenh gaa-ayaad miinawaa wiiwan, miinawaa niizh ikwewag iko imaa gii-ayaawag, oshkiniigikweg.
Mii eta go gaa-tashiyaang imaa, miinawaa bezhig a'aw ninoshenh.

paragraph.text_eng: Along toward spring, she, my grandmother, said, "Oh, goodness, we'll leave tomorrow." My, I was really happy. I barely remember it. I was really happy that we were coming to live in the woods. There was still a lot of snow.

sentence.sent_text: Mii azhigwa ini-ziigwaninig, ini-ziigwaninig, "Oo, yay," ikido, "mii waabang ji-maajaayaang," ikido.
Niminwendam, niminwendam megwayaak ji-bi-daayaang, megwayaak ji-bi-daayaang.

paragraph.text_eng: "Harness the horses," she told the women. Well I always tagged along watching how things were done. It was at dawn that morning when she got up and tied everything on: blankets, things to eat, and even a shovel that time. When she loaded all of it up, we drove off in the morning.

sentence.sent_text: Aanish, mii go apane gii-wiiji'iweyaan apane ganawaabiyaan aaniin ezhichigeng.
Azhigwa wayaabang, azhigwa gigizheb goshkozi, akina gegoo gii-onapidood, waabooyaanan miinawaa ge-bi-miijiyaang, mangaanibaajigan gaye gii-ayaamagad i'iw apii.

paragraph.text_eng: About noon we arrived at the point called Iskigamiziganing 'The Sap Boiling Place'. That's where her storage lodge was located. There were lots of sap buckets there and we had buried the kettles there underneath. Nobody ever bothered the kettles.

sentence.sent_text: Ingoji go nayaawakweg, mii imaa gii-pagamidaabii'iweyaang imaa neyaashiing, iskigamiziganing izhi-wiindemagad.
Biskitenaaganan imaa niibowa atewan, miinawaa ingiw akikoog anaamayi'ii ingii-ningwa'waanaanig.
Gaawiin wiikaa awiiya ogii-pabaamenimaasiin iniw akikoon.

paragraph.text_eng: "Oh, hurry up!" she said. I think there was a wigwam frame there. I barely remember it. She only had to pull the wigwam frame upright and tie it tight all around. There were cattail mats there and birch bark roofing rolls. "Hurry up," she said. "Shovel it out," she said and the women shovelled -- there wasn't any man around, so they shovelled it out. When it was nearly evening, they built a big fire and the snow melted.

sentence.sent_text: Mii eta go badakibidood, babaa-mamaashkawapidood wiigiwaamaak.
Mii go imaa iniw apakweshkwayan gii-ayaag, miinawaa go wiigwaasabakwayan.
Mangaanibaajigewaad ingiw ikwewag, gaawiin inini gii-ayaasiin, mangaanibaadamowaad.
Mii azhigwa gegaa onaagoshig gichi-boodawewaad gaye ningizod a'aw goon.

paragraph.text_eng: Then it was evening and they put everything in place, covering the wigwam with mats. The old lady really was industrious and made sleeping platforms. She used sticks. When it got dark, we slept there on them. The ground was wet.

sentence.sent_text: Miish azhigwa onaagoshig, azhigwa, miish i'iw akina gii-atoowaad gii-apakwaadamowaad i'iw wiigiwaam.
Miish miinawaa azhigwa gii-wenda-ginzhizhawizid a'aw mindimooyenh, miinawaa azhigwa gaa-izhi-desa'oniked.
Miish imaa azhigwa debikak, mii imaa gii-nibaayaang.

paragraph.text_eng: When it was morning again, she said, "The trees aren't running yet," and shook out the sap buckets, shook everything out and washed the kettles. They were getting ready. The time came that she was looking at the trees every day. Then it was time: "Goodness gracious, hurry, the maples are running just fast," she said. The women had cut wood beforehand. They had a saw. They had piled up a whole lot of firewood.

sentence.sent_text: Gegizhebaawagak azhigwa miinawaa, "Mii jibwaa-onjigaag iniw mitigoon," ikido, bawinang iniw obiskitenaaganan, akina gegoo gii-pawinang, miinawaa akikoog, giziibiiginaawaad iniw akikoon.
Ingoding igo azhigwa, apane endaso-giizhig igo waabamaad iniw mitigoon.
Ingoding igo azhigwa, "Way, yay, wewiib enda-gizhigaawan iniw ininaatigoon," ikido.
Mii go gaye giizhaa gaa-izhi-manisewaad ingiw ikwewag.

paragraph.text_eng: The wigwam was big. On the other side of the fire were my uncle, his wife, and one little girl. She was small. They arrived sometime after we had done the building. They too drove a team and brought hay to feed the horses.

sentence.sent_text: Agaamindesiing mii iwidi gii-ayaawaad a'aw inzhishenh iniw wiiwan miinawaa bezhig ikwezens.
Gaye wiinawaa gii-pi-bagamidaabii'iwewag, ingiw bebezhigooganzhiig, mashkosiwan imaa gii-piidood ashamaawaad bebezhigooganzhiin.

paragraph.text_eng: "Oh, my," she said, "those trees are running now. Come around with me, Naawakamigook!" she said to me. "Carry those sap buckets!" she said. This is what she did: when she went up to a tree, she carried on her back the taps she had made -- she had a long skirt on -- I was watching her and she got wet -- their skirts were so long then -- she got really wet, and as I watched her, she went around tapping trees; as for me, I carried along the bundles of sap buckets, ten to a bundle.

sentence.sent_text: Miish i'iw ezhichiged, mii bezhig iniw mitigoon ezhi-naazikawaad, ezhi-ozhitood i'iw ayi'ii, iniw ayi'iin negwaakwaanan, ezhi-bimoondang iko, gichi-ginwegambizod ganawaabamag iko, gichi-nisaabaawed, gichi-gagaanwegadinig iniw ogoodaasiwaan gichi-nisaabaawed, ganawaabamag iko babaa-ozhiga'iged, gaye niin ezhi-bimiwidooyaan midaaso-okwapidewan biskitenaaganan.

paragraph.text_eng: We looked to make sure they wouldn't leak and if they did, we stuck pitch on them. "Place them carefully," she told me. "Don't spill any," she said. "It's said that long ago they never spilled any sap. Don't spill any of that sap," she said to me. She got lots of sap then.

sentence.sent_text: Mii go ezhi-waabandamaang ji-onjigaasinog mii onjigaag, bigiw imaa ezhi-agokanangid.
Miish azhigwa, gichi-niibowa azhigwa gii-ayaang i'iw ziinzibaakwadwaaboo.

paragraph.text_eng: There were barrels there called atoobaanan. In the evening, when the sap buckets were full, the women carried the sap and poured it into them, straining the sap through a doth. In the morning there were three barrels full, so they hung the kettles. They boiled sap inside, not outside; when they boiled sap, they put it there.

sentence.sent_text: Mii gaye iniw makakosagoon atoobaanan iidog izhi-wiindewan.

Azhigwa onaagoshig, mii go azhigwa mooshkinebiig iniw ayi'iin biskitenaaganan, azhigwa naadoobiiwaad ingiw ikwewag imaa ziiginamowaad, ayi'ii bagiwayaanish imaa ziikoobiiginamowaad i'iw ziinzibaakwadwaaboo.
Mii azhigwa niswi go mooshkinebiig iniw makakoon waabaninig, ezhi-onakinaawaad.
Biindig igaye dash iskigamizigewag, gaawiin agwajiing, iskigamizigewaad, atoowaad.

paragraph.text_eng: What I did was stand by the fire watching things so they didn't boil over, holding a fir bough, while the women stoked the fire. If it boiled over, I dipped the bough in the kettle. That's what I did all day.

sentence.sent_text: Miish i'iw enanokiiyaan niin, mii ezhi-niibawiyaan jiigishkode ganawaabandamaan gegoo iwidi ziigigamidesinog, ezhi-dakonag zhingobaandag, ikwewag boodawewaad.
Mii go imaa ziigigamideg, mii imaa o-gondaabiiginag zhingobaandag akikong.
Mii eta go enanokiiyaan, mii go gabe-giizhig.

paragraph.text_eng: There was one pail there where they poured what they had when they finished boiling. By night, that single pail, the one that hung last in the row, just the one pail there, was syrup. There was a fire there all night and in the morning they strained it.

sentence.sent_text: Bezhig azhigwa a'aw akik, mii imaa ani-ziiginamowaad i'iw azhigwa ayaamowaad, giizhigamizigewaad.
Bezhig a'aw akik miinawaa dibikak, mii a'aw eshkwegoojing, bezhig iwidi akik eta go, mii i'iw zhiiwaagamizigan.
Gabe-dibik ezhi-ishkodewang imaa miinawaa gigizheb azhigwa ziikoobiiginamowaad i'iw.

paragraph.text_eng: She washed the kettles. "Wash these kettles," she said. And if it rained, then the sap buckets were washed; she was always washing them.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa gimiwang, mii i'iw apii giziibiiginigaadewan iniw ayi'iin biskitenaaganan, apane gii-kiziibiiginang.

paragraph.text_eng: She didn't keep the syrup long. They say that the results of each sugaring should be put away as you go into the boxes, birch bark boxes, so as they sugared off: they put in the sugar.

sentence.sent_text: Mii go ingo-ombigamizigan ikidom, eni-izhi-biina'ang makakong, wiigwaasi-makakong, ombigamizigewaad, eni-izhi-biina'amowaad imaa i'iw ayi'ii, i'iw ziinzibaakwad.

paragraph.text_eng: The storekeeper bought sugar cakes from them. They used to buy flour, tea, lard, whatever they wanted to eat. Those ladies worked hard going to the shore and setting a net through a crack in the ice. They got lots of fish. Then they roasted the fish or fixed them in other ways. They might boil them or roast them by the fire.

sentence.sent_text: Miish ko gii-adaawewaad bakwezhiganan, aniibiish, bimide, waa-miijiwaad.
Miinawaa ingiw ikwewag gii-wenda-ginzhizhawiziwag madaabiiwaad, ezhi-bagida'waawaad daashkikwadininig, mii imaa iniw asabiin onaabiiginaawaad.
Mii ezhi-abwewaad iniw giigoonyan, gaye wii-izhi'aawaad igo.

paragraph.text_eng: Then when we got done boiling sap, there were leaf-buds on the trees. When we got done boiling sap, we gathered everything together, washed the sap buckets, and tied them up. Then they moved camp down to the shore, moved to the lake. We gathered everything up. They lived there by the lake and fished. They used to sell the fish. There were lots of fish. They were given a nickel a pound for walleyes. They were always fishing there by the lake.

sentence.sent_text: Miish azhigwa, miish azhigwa ishkwaagamizigeyaang, miish azhigwa aniibiishensan ayaamagak.
Ishkwaagamizigeyaang, mii ezhi-asiginamaang akina gegoo giziibiiginamaang gaye iniw biskitenaaganan ezhi-dakobidooyaang.
Miish imaa endaawaad imaa jiigibiig, wewebanaabiiwaad.

paragraph.text_eng: Then in berry-picking time, they picked blueberries. But first we went home. First the old lady went to do the planting. Her garden was big. The garden the old lady planted was big.

sentence.sent_text: Mii azhigwa mawinzong, azhigwa mawinzowaad iniw miinan.
Miinawaa go da-o-gitige akawe, o-gitiged, a'aw mindimooyenh o-gitiged.
Gii-michaani iko ogitigaan a'aw mindimooyenh gaa-izhi-gitiged.

paragraph.text_eng: Then it was close to the middle of the summer. Some of the potatoes were full-grown and we left to go around picking berries. We used horses and went to pick at the Mississippi. They took along a tent. We went berry-picking in order to sell the blueberries. Then they bought flour, sugar, tea, coffee, and whatever they wanted to eat. And after we got through picking berries, we brought some of them back there. My grandmother, or maybe my aunt, canned them. She canned everything.

sentence.sent_text: Miish aanind, miish azhigwa opiniin giizhiginid miinawaa ezhi-maajaayaang, babaa-mawinzoyaang.
Mii go ingiw bebezhigooganzhiig gichi-ziibiing iko ingii-izhi-mawinzomin.
Mii iwidi mawinzoyaang waa-adaawaageyaang iniw miinan.
Miish akeyaa bakwezhiganan ezhi-adaawewaad, miinawaa ziinzibaakwad, miinawaa adaawewaad aniibiish, makade-mashkikiwaaboo, ge-wii-miijiwaad igo.
Mii ezhi-gibaakobidood nookomis maagizhaa gaye ninoshenh.

paragraph.text_eng: That's how they lived. She canned everything. I picked berries too. I made everything.
And a long time ago we used to live far away. It was about thirty miles as the white man would say.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa mewinzha ko iwidi waasa ingii-taamin.
Ingoji go nisimidana daso-diba'igan daa-ikido a'aw gichi-mookomaan.

paragraph.text_eng: They used to drive horses when we came here to Iskigamiziganing 'The Sap Boiling Place', as it was called. That's where the old lady's sap-boiling lodge was. She made it. I don't remember how she made that sap-boiling lodge. It looked like a house.

sentence.sent_text: Bebezhigooganzhiin iko ogii-odaabii'aawaan, miish imaa ba-izhaayaang imaa iskigamiziganing gii-izhi-wiinde.
Mii imaa gii-ayaanig i'iw odiskigamizigewigamig a'aw mindimooyenh.

paragraph.text_eng: In the middle she put up what's called an iskigamiziganaak 'sap boiling frame'. She put up four sticks, [two] on each end, they put them up. They laid a stick across [each set of end poles]. Then they chopped some short sticks and carefully peeled them [to go over the cross sticks]. The kettle hangers were [attached to them] there. The kettle hangers were really nice.

sentence.sent_text: Miish imaa naawayi'ii ezhi-onakidood i'iw iskigamiziganaak ezhi-wiindeg.
Niiwin eyishkwe-ayi'ii obadakinaanan iniw mitigoon, obadakinaawaan.
Miish miinawaa odadaakwaakoga'aanaawaan wawiinge gaye obishagikodaanaawaan iniw mitigoon.

paragraph.text_eng: That's where the kettles hung. One kettle hung there at the front. That's where they kept pouring it as it thickened into syrup. That's how they made syrup.

sentence.sent_text: Miish imaa ani-ziiginamowaad apane go imaa ini zhiiwaagamideg i'iw.

paragraph.text_eng: Then when it was done boiling, the sugar thickened into syrup.

sentence.sent_text: Miish azhigwa giizhigamideg, mii i'iw ziinzibaakwad, ziinzibaakwad azhigwa zhiiwaagamideg.

paragraph.text_eng: They didn't just take it off the fire. The kettle was heavy. The syrup was heavy. Holding the [short peeled] stick on both ends, they slid it, slid it along on a stick, slid the kettle along on a stick. It didn't get burnt there then, but the other ones were left to boil.

sentence.sent_text: Miish eyiidawayi'ii ezhi-minjiminamowaad i'iw mitig, ozhooshkonaanaawaa, ozhooshkwaakonaanaawaa, ozhooshkwaakonaanaawaan iniw akikoon.
Miish gaawiin jaagizosiin imaa; ingiwedig-sh aanind endakamidemagak.

paragraph.text_eng: They used a rag to strain the syrup. They were always doing that.

sentence.sent_text: Mii i'iw ayi'ii ziinzibaakwadwaaboo, oziikoobiiginaanaawaa gaye, ayi'ii bagiwayaanish i'iw odaabajitoonaawaa ziikoobiiginamowaad i'iw zhiiwaagamizigan.

paragraph.text_eng: That sap-boiling lodge, as it was called, was there a long time. I never see any of them anywhere today.

sentence.sent_text: Ginwenzh imaa gii-ayaamagad i'iw iskigamizigewigamig izhi-wiinde.
Gaawiin noongom wiikaa ingoji niwaabandanziin geyaabi, mii iniw.

paragraph.text_eng: Every spring when they came over, when she came over, all she [grandmother] had to do was tie it up using the inner bark of the basswood and cover it. If there was a lot of snow there, they shovelled it out again. They didn't lie down to sleep on the bare ground. She made a platform just like a bed. The ground was wet as long as it kept thawing out there inside. Well, they kept boiling sap there through the night. Long ago the Indian didn't boil sap outside.

sentence.sent_text: Mii go endaso-ziigwaninig, bi-maajaad, bi-maajaawaad, bi-maajaayaang, mii eta go datakobidood wiigob ge-aabajitood miinawaa apakwaadang.
Giishpin-sh goon niibowa abid imaa, omangaanibaadaanaawaa miinawaa.
Mii nibiiwakamigaag eni-apiichi-ningideg i'iw ayi'ii, i'iw ayi'ii aki, imaa biindig.
Aanish, mii go apane, mii go gaye niibaa-dibik ezhi-iskigamizigewaad.
Gaawiin agwajiing gii-tazhi iskigamizigesiin mewinzha anishinaabe.

paragraph.text_eng: A long time ago my grandmother and I used to boil maple sap. When she sugared off: I stood there. I dipped in that little carved paddle called the neyakokwaanens.

sentence.sent_text: Mii i'iw ombigamiziged, mii imaa niibawiyaan.
Mii i'iw neyakokwaanens izhi-wiinde, jekaagaminamaan i'iw.

paragraph.text_eng: When the sugar started to get done, "Get the ice!" So I took off running down to the shore where the ice piles up to get some.

sentence.sent_text: Miish azhigwa wii-kiizhideg i'iw ziinzibaakwad, "Mikwam naazh!"
Mii ezhi-maajiibatooyaan iwidi agamiing, mikwam okoshing naanag.

paragraph.text_eng: She recognized just what the sugar looked like when it was about to finish cooking. She used a wooden ladle to scoop it out. She scooped it up when it sugared. Then she poured it on the ice. My, I was really happy making that maple sugar taffy and eating it. That's what my grandmother always did.

sentence.sent_text: Mii azhigwa wii-kiizhidenig, onisidawinaan ezhi-naagwadinig i'iw ayi'ii ziinzibaakwad wii-kiizhidenig.
Mii ezhi-gwaaba'ang mii i'iw ayi'ii ziinzibaakwad ombigamiziged.
Waa, niminwendam, niminwendam gichi-niibowa ozhitooyaan i'iw bigiwizigan, miijiyaan.
Mii i'iw apane gaa-izhichiged a'aw nookomis.

paragraph.text_eng: She used birch bark then to make sugar molds, forming the bark into cones. That's what she used when she cast sugar cones, which used to be called zhiishiigwaansag. Those were the cakes that formed when they poured it into the bark.

sentence.sent_text: Miish i'iw ezhi-ziiga'iganiked, wiigwaasan-sh iko ogii-aabajitoonan, wiigwaas ezhi-bajiishkinang.
Miish i'iw ayaabajitood i'iw ayaad, ziiga'iged iniw ziiga'igaansan zhiishiigwaansag gii-izhinikaazowag iko.
Mii iniw ziiga'iganan ziiga'igeng imaa wiigwaasing.

paragraph.text_eng: When the boiled sugar hardened, she poured it into the sugaring trough and stirred to granulate it, making it into sugar. There was a lot, a whole lot of maple sugar there.

sentence.sent_text: Miish azhigwa naseyaawangwaaning oziiginaan i'iw azhigwa mashkawi-ayaanig i'iw ayi'ii ombigamizigan, naseyaawangwed, i'iw ziinzibaakwad ozhitood.

paragraph.text_eng: And then she said this to me, "Wash the kettle, Naawakamigook! Don't spill it! Take care of it!" she told me. So I washed the treaty kettle using __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ hot water. That's what I was up to as she gathered things up.

sentence.sent_text: Gizhaagamideg nibi indaabajitoon giziibiiginag __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ a'aw okaadakik, ezhi-giziibiiginag.

paragraph.text_eng: She sugared off every time it boiled down, sometimes twice if it was a nice day, if it was clear in the morning. "That sugar is nice," she said when she sugared off in clear weather.

sentence.sent_text: Mii endaso-ombigamiziged, aangodinong gaye niizhing ombigamiziged, giishpin mino-giizhigadinig, gigizheb mizhakwadinig.

paragraph.text_eng: And then as I tended the kettle, I'd get a lot of kettle-washing liquid, called giziibiiginakokwaanaaboo. It was really sweet.

sentence.sent_text: Miish eni-izhi-ganawendamaan akikong, miish i'iw niibowa ayaamaan i'iw giziibiiginakokwaanaaboo gii-izhi-wiindemagad.

paragraph.text_eng: "Naawakamigook, you sugar off too!"
I must have tried it. I sugared off the kettle washing liquid, and I too did the boiling. And then I sugared off and I too made sugar cones. They weren't black. They were nice.

sentence.sent_text: Mii ezhi-ombigamizamaan i'iw giziibiiginakokwaanaaboo, iskigamizamaan gaye niin.
Miish o'o ombigamizamaan, ozhitooyaan gaye niin ziiga'igaansan.

paragraph.text_eng: She was always cleaning the kettle. That's what I did too.
That's it.

When I was small, my grandmother used to come over here to boil sap. I was the only one when I was a little girl, when I was a naughty little girl. Sometimes while they were sleeping or maybe while they were hauling sap, I'd steal the sugaring trough. Long ago there was a puddle there with lots of water in it, so I stole the sugaring trough. I must not have been very big.

sentence.sent_text: Mii eta go gii-pezhigoyaan, gii-ikwezensiwiyaan, gii-ikwezhenzhishiwiyaan.
Miish iko ayi'ii, nibaawaad ayaangodinong maagizhaa gaye naadoobiiwaad, mii ezhi-gimoodiyaan i'iw ayi'ii naseyaawangwaan.
Imaa ayi'iing waanashkaag imaa gii-wenda-nibiikaa mewinzha ezhi-gimoodiyaan naseyaawangwaan.
Miish iidog, gaawiin dash iidog ingii-mindidosiin.

paragraph.text_eng: The trough wasn't very big. I used to get in that trough and paddle it around in the puddle. Then when I heard them boiling sap down and wondering where they had misplaced it, I'd hide. Sometimes I got a licking when it was found out that I'd stolen the sugar trough for paddling around there in the mud puddle.

sentence.sent_text: Mii ko ezhi-booziyaan imaa babaamishkaayaan imaa ayi'iing waanashkobiiyaag i'iw naseyaawangwaan.
Azhigwa madwe-ombigamizigewaad madwe-wanitoowaad iko aandi i'iw, ezhi-gaazoyaan.
Ayaangodinong igaye imbapakite'igaaz giishpin mikigaadeg imaa gimoodiyaan naseyaawangwaan, baamishkaayaan imaa megwejiishkiwag.

paragraph.text_eng: Long ago my grandmother used to boil sap here, a very long time ago. This I remember.

sentence.sent_text: Mewinzha imaa ko gii-pi-dazhi-iskigamizige a'aw nookomis, gichi-mewinzha go.

paragraph.text_eng: "The children fast along toward spring," she said. When I got up in the morning, she said to me, "Naawakamigook, get some charcoal. Rub it on your face," so I rubbed the charcoal on my face.

sentence.sent_text: Gigizheb ingoding goshkoziyaan, "Naawakamigook, mamoon akakanzhe," indig.

paragraph.text_eng: "Don't take a taste of anything," she said. "And don't chew on twigs either. The sun will see you for sure. The sun is watching you," she said to me.
I didn't have anything to eat as I went along. I left from Iskigamiziganing, as the sugar camp is called.

sentence.sent_text: Miish igo imaa iskigamiziganing izhi-wiindeg imaa, gaa-izhi-maajaayaan.

paragraph.text_eng: I was just feeling sad. I didn't eat. I got hungry hanging around there, so I took a twig. The twig, a maple twig, was kind of big, so I broke it in half. It was sweet. I wanted to chew on it and I got behind a tree so the sun couldn't see me because I was afraid. I set off for the point where the big rock sat. The rock that was there was very big. The Indians always take tobacco there. I don't know why they do but they make an offering of tobacco to that rock.

sentence.sent_text: Imbakade babaa-ayaayaan imaa, mii ko ezhi-mamooyaan mitigoons.
Gomaa go inigokwaa i'iw mitigoons, ayi'ii i'iw aninaatigoons i'iw.
Mii i'iw waa-shaashaagwandamaan, ezhi-aagawewetaayaan imaa ji-ganawaabamisig a'aw giizis, aagawewetaayaan imaa mitigong, gaa-izhi-zegiziyaan.
Gaa-izhi-maajaayaan miinawaa imaa-sh neyaashiiwang abi gichi-asin.
Anishinaabeg imaa asemaan odizhiwinaawaan apane imaa, iniw asemaan.
Amanj iidog i'iw izhichigewaad, biindaakoonaawaad imaa iniw asiniin, iniw asemaan.

paragraph.text_eng: I was sitting there on top of the rock watching the ice. The ice was just about broken up. It got real hot while I was sitting there. I saw some plug tobacco there and it looked good to me, so I took that plug and bit off a piece. My, that tobacco tasted good to me -- oh, I was spitting hard. A little while later I started to get dizzy from it. I was just sleepy and I wanted to puke, so I lay down on the top of the rock.

sentence.sent_text: Mii dash i'iw nanaamadabiyaan imaa agiji-asin, ganawaabamag a'aw mikwam.
Gegaa go azhigwa niigoshkaa a'aw mikwam.
Ingii-waabamaa imaa, niwenda-minwaabamaa meziwezid asemaa, ezhi-mamag mii a'aw meziwezid, bakwemag.
Wa, niwenda-minopwaa, mii a'aw asemaa -- wa gichi-zaziikoyaan.
Ingoding igo baanimaa go wenji-giiwashkweyaan, giiwashkweyaan.
Niwenda-giikiibingwash, niwii-shishigagowe gaye, gaa-izhi-gawishimoyaan imaa agiji-asin.

paragraph.text_eng: I must have gone to sleep there. The tobacco made me dizzy. In the evening, towards evening, I went home.

sentence.sent_text: Azhigwa wenaagoshig, eni-onaagoshig, azhigwa giiweyaan, giiweyaan azhigwa.

paragraph.text_eng: She must have made a little cup of birch bark, just a tiny cup, and she gave me a drink of water. When I finished drinking, she took it outside, hung it up, and made a single mark on it with charcoal.

sentence.sent_text: Enda-agaasaani i'iw ayi'ii, ayi'ii wiigwaasing iidog gaa-ozhitoogwen onaagaans, enda-agaasaani onaagaans, mina'id i'iw ayi'ii nibi.
Eshkwaa-minikweyaan, agwajiing gaa-izhiwidood, gii-agoodood gii-peshibii'ang akakanzhe aabiding.

paragraph.text_eng: "It's two days," she said, "that you'll fast," and I lay down again. In the morning when I got up again, she didn't feed me.

sentence.sent_text: Azhigwa miinawaa gegizhebaawagak gweshkoziyaan, mii gaawiin indashamigosiin.

paragraph.text_eng: I was kind of glad [that I was fasting] as there certainly was a lot of work to be done in getting ready for boiling sap. There was woodcutting to be done. But I was being told to fast.

sentence.sent_text: Niminwendam, niminwendam-sh igo gaye, booch onzaam niibowa inanokiim azhigwa ozhiitaang iskigamizigeng.

paragraph.text_eng: I got scared remembering about how I chewed on the twig and put tobacco in my mouth. I fasted for two days. Then when it got dark, the old lady again fed me wild rice.

sentence.sent_text: Mii gaa-izhi-segiziyaan i'iw mikwendamaan i'iw gii-shaashaagwandamaan mitigoons, miinawaa asemaa gii-agwanemag imaa.
Azhigwa eni-dibikak, mii gaa-izhi-ashamid a'aw mindimooyenh, manoomin miinawaa ayi'ii.

paragraph.text_eng: We used to have an old man there and he began telling me stories, telling me all sorts of legends. I don't remember what he told me about.

sentence.sent_text: Akiwenzii ko ingii-ayaawaanaan, ezhi-maadaajimod dadibaajimotawid, anooji-gegoo aadizookawid.

paragraph.text_eng: That's all I remember of what I did.

sentence.sent_text: Mii eta go minik miinawaa gekendamaan gaa-izhichigeyaan.

paragraph.text_eng: Again I barely remember about long ago. All I remember is sitting on the shore. Maybe they were fishing or had just finished boiling sap. The lake was open anyway.

sentence.sent_text: Mii eta go imaa gikendamaan namadabiyaan jiigibiig.
Maagizhaa gaye gaa-wewebanaabiiwaagwen, maagizhaa gaye gaa-ishkwaa-iskigamizigewaagwen.

paragraph.text_eng: I was sitting there watching a big boat go across the middle of the lake. I don't know where that boat was going. There were pine trees in bundles. I was watching men standing on them.

sentence.sent_text: Mii imaa niibawiwaad imaa, ganawaabamagwaa ingiw.

paragraph.text_eng: So once I asked the old lady, "Did there used to be a big boat?" I said to her.

sentence.sent_text: Miish ingoding gaa-izhi-gagwejimag a'aw mindimooyenh, "Gichi-jiimaan ina ko gii-ayaamagad?"

paragraph.text_eng: "Yes," she said, "long ago there were lots of pine trees here at Mille Lacs Lake. There were so many pines that it was dark. The fallen pine needles lay a foot or two deep. The fallen pine needles lay so deep that sometimes you couldn't hear anyone coming. There were leaves and big trees. There used to be a steamboat here," she said.

sentence.sent_text: "Enyan'," ikido, "mewinzha giiwenh gii-paatayiinowag zhingwaakwag omaa Misi-zaaga'iganiing.
Mii go gaa-izhi-gashki-dibiki-ayaag gaa-apiichi-baatayiinowaad ingiw zhingwaakwag.
Ingodozid, ingodozid maagizhaa gaye niizhozid apiichishinoog ingiw zhingwaakwaandagoog, binaakwiiwaad.
Aangodinong, gaawiin awiiya gidaa-noondawaasiin bimweweshing, apiichishinowaad ingiw zhingwaakwaandagoog, binaakwiiwaad.
Miish ishkode-jiimaan iko omaa gaa-ayaamagad," gii-ikido.

paragraph.text_eng: Over there -- I don't know what they call that river there at Vineland where it starts -- that's where the big boat went. Long ago that river must have been big.

sentence.sent_text: Iwidi-sh iidog ayi'ii -- amanj ezhinikaadegwen i'iw ziibi imaa Zaagiing wenji-maajitigweyaag -- mii giiwenh imaa gaa-ini-ipideg i'iw gichi-jiimaan.

paragraph.text_eng: There was a sawmill there at Onamia, which the Indians call Gibaakwa'iganing 'At the Dam'. That's where they used to take those pines long ago. I wonder where that old steamship went to. I don't know where it might have been taken.

sentence.sent_text: Miish iwidi Gibaakwa'iganing odizhi-wiindaanaawaa anishinaabeg, miish iwidi gii-ayaad a'aw daashkiboojigan.
Miish iko iwidi gaa-izhiwinindwaa ingiw zhingwaakwag gichi-mewinzha.

paragraph.text_eng: And a long time ago my late grandmother used to tell me all sorts of things. I only remember some of them.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa mewinzha a'aw iko mindimooyenyiban, akina gegoo ingii-waawiindamaag.

paragraph.text_eng: She said, " 'One should not chop the sap boiling frame for firewood,' they used to say, so we were forbidden to chop up the sap boiling poles for firewood.

sentence.sent_text: Miish i'iw gaa-ikidod, "«Mii i'iw ayi'ii iskigamiziganaak,» gii-ikidowag iko, «gaawiin giiwenh awiiya odaa-manisaadanziin i'iw,» gaa-izhi-gina'amaagooyaang iko gete-iskigamiziganaatigoon ji-manisaadamaang."

paragraph.text_eng: "If anyone chopped up the sap boiling poles for firewood, he'd break his leg. There was a prohibition long ago against the chopping up of the old sap boiling poles for firewood."

sentence.sent_text: "Mii giiwenh awiiya manisaadang mii iniw iskigamiziganaatigoon ezhi-bookogaadeshing.
Mii gaa-izhi-gina'amaading mewinzha ji-manisaadanziing iniw gete-iskigamiziganaatigoon.

paragraph.text_eng: It was up here -- I don't know what I should call it -- the next point over, where the old lady was boiling sap. My uncle didn't come that time. I barely remember when we were boiling sap over there. There were just the two young women, me, and the old lady boiling sap. It used to be that long ago those wigwams were long, they were long lodges. They used to boil sap there inside. They never boiled sap outside. There were birch bark coverings and, down at the bottom, cattail mats.

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa, mii i'iw omaa akeyaa -- amanj iidog ge-izhinikaadamowaambaanen -- omaa neyaashiiwan iwidi iskigamiziged a'aw mindimooyenh.
Gaawiin a'aw inzhishenh gii-pi-izhaasiin mii i'iw apii.
Agaawaa go, agaawaa go ingezikwendaan iwidi iskigamizigeyaang.
Mii eta go niizh oshkiniigikweg, niizh ingiw oshkiniigikweg, miinawaa gaye niin miinawaa-sh a'aw mindimooyenh, iskigamizigewaad.
Miish ko mewinzha iniw wiigiwaaman ko gii-kagaanwaawan, gagaanoondewan.
Mii ingiw wiigwaasabakwayan miinawaa-sh ingiw apakweshkwayag imaa, imaa michayi'ii.

paragraph.text_eng: It was along towards spring. They were still washing the sap buckets -- they would wash everything they used -- and then they made a little domed lodge. They put everything in there when they got through boiling sap. And when it was spring again, they came back and fixed up their wigwam.

sentence.sent_text: Aaniish naa geyaabi ogii-kiziibiiginaanaawaan iko mii iniw biskitenaaganan -- akina gegoo ayaabajitoowaad owii-kiziibiiginaanaawaan -- miinawaa gaa-izhi-ozhitoowaad waaginogaanens.
Miish imaa akina gegoo biina'amowaad, ishkwaagamizigewaad.
Mii miinawaa ziigwang, mii miinawaa imaa ba-izhaawaad miinawaa nanaa'itoowaad owiigiwaamiwaa.

paragraph.text_eng: We were staying there and were then going to gather things up. It was after sap-boiling time. When it starts to go bad, they wouldn't take any sap; they quit at the last run. And then, oh goodness, thunder, it was really rumbling and the thunder was coming. Goodness, the women were __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ really scared, really scared because there were lots of trees around.

sentence.sent_text: Miish imaa gii-ayaayaang, miish azhigwa wii-asiginamowaad.
Gaawiin gaye ani-maanaadadinig, ogii-mamoosiinaawaan i'iw ziinzibaakwadwaaboo, ishkwaagaanig, mii ezhi-ishkwaataawaad.
Miish azhigwa, oo waa, animikiig -- gii-wenda-zegwewemagad -- __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ bi-noondaagoziwaad ingiw animikiig.
Waa, enda-zegiziwag, enda-zegiziwag, mii ingiw ikwewag, niibowa mitigoon.

paragraph.text_eng: "Oh, no, my daughter," she said, "come on, come on, let's go to that house." There was a house nearby where a white man was staying. "Let's go to that house," she said. They were friends with the white people living there, so they just started running there. There was a swing hanging there on a big tree. The white man's grandchildren must come and visit them. A swing hung there. That's where I started running to. Well, it was thundering, the sound of the thunder was coming. That's where I was running to.

sentence.sent_text: "Oo, yay indaanis," ikido, "daga naa, daga naa izhaadaa imaa waakaa'iganing."
Besho imaa waakaa'igan, gichi-mookomaan ko gii-ayaa.
Ogii-nagadenimaawaan gichi-mookomaanan imaa gaa-taanijin, gaa-izhi-maajiiba'idiyaang iwidi ezhaayaang.
Ayi'ii ko wewebizon imaa gii-agoodemagad gichi-mitigong, wewebizon imaa.
Iniw ko oozhishenyan iko wa'aw gichi-mookomaan ba-mawadisigowaagwen.
Aaniish naa animikiikaag, iwidi biidwewidamoog animikiig.

paragraph.text_eng: "Naawakamigook, don't, hurry," they said to me in vain. I was starting to run there and I leapt on and swung hard. All of a sudden there was a clap of thunder. That's the last I remember. It was just like little bells ringing. All of a sudden I came to and thought I was sitting by a window. That's all, I don't know what happened to me. That's all I remember about when the lightning struck long ago where we were boiling sap. I still don't remember when we moved camp. I don't know how big I was.

sentence.sent_text: Mii go imaa eni-apatooyan ko akawe ezhi-wawenabibagizoyaan imaa, gichi-wewebizoyaan.
Baanimaa go naa gichi-baashkakwa'amowaad ingiw animikiig.
Baanimaa go miinawaa gikendamaan waasechiganing ninamadab indinendam, jiigayi'ii indinendam.
Mii eta go, amanj-sh iidog gaa-izhiwebiziwaanen.
Mii eta go imaa minik gezikwendamaan, gichi-besho gii-bapakite'igewaad ingiw manidoog, mewinzha, mewinzha mii imaa gii-iskigamizigeyaang.
Gaawiin geyaabi ingikendanziin amanj iidog apii gaa-koziwaangen.

paragraph.text_eng: Long ago she got bulrushes from the lake. "In June," she used to say, "before the middle of the summer."

sentence.sent_text: Miinawaa mewinzha gichigamiiwashkoon mamood zaaga'iganiing, miish iniw.

paragraph.text_eng: She put the tobacco out when she wanted to get bulrushes. "No one is supposed to take them otherwise," she used to say.

sentence.sent_text: Mii asemaan ezhi-bagidinaad, azhigwa wii-mamood iniw ayi'iin gichigamiiwashkoon.

paragraph.text_eng: I always watched what she did with great interest. She got in the canoe, a birch bark canoe. Then she pulled up the gichigamiiwashkoon, as they are called.

sentence.sent_text: Miish i'iw jiimaaning-sh, boozi wiigwaasi-jiimaaning gaye.
Mii ezhi-bakwajibidood, mii iniw gichigamiiwashkoon, ikidowag, izhinikaadenig.

paragraph.text_eng: She pulled up a lot of them, took what she got to shore, and tied them up. She tied them in bundles of about thirty. Then she cut them off at the roots.

sentence.sent_text: Mii azhigwa niibowa ezhi-bakwajibidood, mii ezhi-ayaad ezhi-agwaasidood, mii ezhi-maawandoopidood.
Mii ingoji go nisimidana, ingoji go odizhi-maawandoopidoonan.

paragraph.text_eng: I used to sit there eating them. But she forbid me to do that. "Don't eat much!" she said to me. Bulrush roots taste real good.

sentence.sent_text: Mii dash imaa namadabiyaan iko maamiijiyaan mii iniw.

paragraph.text_eng: I can barely remember long ago -- I don't know how big I was -- going down to the shore. There was a canoe there so I got in it. I must have climbed down to the far end. I don't remember much.

sentence.sent_text: Mewinzha agaawaa ingezikwendaan -- amanj iidog gaa-iniginiwaanen -- madaabiiyaan.

paragraph.text_eng: When I took a look, the boat was far out and I heard some ladies, maybe three or four of them, my grandmother and my aunt, two of my aunts, running towards me, crying as they came, some of them running right into the water, and so I got scared.

sentence.sent_text: Imaa inaabiyaan igo, waasa azhigwa ayaamagad i'iw jiimaan, noondawagwaa ikwewag, niswi maagizhaa gaye niiwin, nookomis miinawaa go ninoshenh, miinawaa go ninoshenyag niizh, biijiba'idiwaad, bi-mawiwaad, aanind biidaadagaaziiba'idiwaad, gaa-izhi-zegiziyaan.

paragraph.text_eng: I remember that I was scared. I must have jumped. Then I remember looking at fish of all different colors. They were sunfish. Sometimes they came real close and looked at me. That's all I have remembered. I must have been picked up out of the water.

sentence.sent_text: Baanimaa dash igo miinawaa gikendamaan iwidi ganawaabamagwaa ingiw giigoonyag, eniwek igo naa anooj ezhi-naagoziwaad.
Mii eta go imaa minik gaa-gikendamaan.

paragraph.text_eng: A long time ago, we lived at Portage Lake in the spring after she [my grandmother] finished boiling sap. She hurried to plant the garden. The old lady planted all kinds of things in that garden she had. When she got through planting, she left for here at Mille Lacs Lake where we went fishing. The fish used to be bought from them. All that old lady did was work for herself.

sentence.sent_text: Mewinzha, mii go iwidi Gabekanaansing gii-taayaang, ani-ziigwang ishkwaa-iskigamiziged.
Anooj igo gegoo bagidinang i'iw gitigaan ogii-ayaan a'aw mindimooyenh.
Mii ba-izhi-maajaad, ishkwaa-bagidiniged bi-wewebanaabiiyaang imaa Misi-zaaga'iganiing.
Mii eta go gaa-izhi-izhichiged a'aw mindimooyenyiban gii-anokiitaazod.

paragraph.text_eng: I used to get real tired as we fished all day. We caught lots of fish. Then she cleaned them. She took the guts out and when she finished cleaning them, she took them on her back and went and sold them. The one that bought the walleyes, at five cents a pound, was called Giigoonh-kiwenzhiinh 'Old Man Fish'.

sentence.sent_text: Giigoonh-kiwenzhiinh gii-inaa ko a'aw gaa-adaawed iniw, aabita-zhooniyaans ingo-dibaabiishkoojigan iniw ogaawan.

paragraph.text_eng: After about a week or ten days, when she thought she had enough, we came back home. We drove a team to Portage Lake. The garden was just coming up then and all the leaves were fully grown.

sentence.sent_text: Ingoji go ingo-anama'e-giizhigad maagizhaa gaye midaasogon debiseyendang, ani-dagoshinaang iwidi endaayaang.
Mii azhigwa zaagiging gitigaan, akina go gegoo azhigwa giizhibagaag iniw aniibiishan.

paragraph.text_eng: She hurried to hoe, to hoe the potatoes, and early in the morning before the sun was up, she woke me to go and weed the garden. I used to cry. "She's mean to me," I thought.

sentence.sent_text: Mii ezhi-wewiibitaayaang ningwaja'iged, ningwaja'waad igaye opiniin, gichi-gigizheb amadinid jibwaa-mooka'aninig, ji-o-bashkwashkibidoowag i'iw gitigaan.

paragraph.text_eng: "Now that the sun is up, you'd better hurry and go hoe those potatoes before it gets hot," she told me. We had planted all sorts of things.

sentence.sent_text: "Azhigwa mooka'ang jibwaa-gizhaateg wewiib o-ningwaja'," indig iko, "ingiw opiniig!"

paragraph.text_eng: There were two women there as well as me. My namesake's family lived at a different place. They too had a little girl. They said, "Let's go berry-picking at the Mississippi."

sentence.sent_text: Miish ingiw ikwewag iko gii-ayaawag niizh oshkiniigikweg miinawaa-sh gaye niin.
Miinawaa dash a'aw niiyawen'enh bakaan gii-taawag.

paragraph.text_eng: You see, there wasn't enough room in the wagon for us. There wasn't enough room for us in the wagon so we caught two of the horses and they harnessed them when they caught them. We took everything along, kettles, flour, everything they wanted to have to eat.

sentence.sent_text: Nashke dash gaawiin indebashkinesiimin imaa odaabaaning.
Gaawiin indebashkinesiimin imaa ditibidaabaaning, debibinangidwaa niizh ingiw bebezhigooganzhiig, ezhi-debibinaawaad onapinaawaad.
Akina gegoo omaajiidoonaawaan iniw akikoon, bakwezhiganan, akina sa gegoo waa-aabajitoowaad wii-wiisiniwaad.

paragraph.text_eng: So my namesake, my uncle, went by canoe, they went by canoe. I don't know which way they paddled, which way he paddled. He used a canoe. They went through Bay Lake and over there somewhere they portaged the canoe to the Mississippi. We met them over there at the Mississippi somewhere.

sentence.sent_text: Mii ezhi-bimishkaad, mii a'aw niiyawen'enh, inzhishenh, mii ezhi-bimishkaawaad.
Miish imaa amanj iidog akeyaa gaa-ini-ayina'owaagwen, gaa-ini-ayina'ogwen.
Zezabegamaag akeyaa gii-ini-izhaawag miinawaa iwidi Zezabegamaag, mii miinawaa iwidi ingoji gaa-izhi-gakiiwewidood i'iw jiimaan, miish iwidi Gichi-ziibiing.
Miish iwidi gii-nagishkawangidwaa, iwidi Gichi-ziibiing, ingoji go iwidi.

paragraph.text_eng: It was towards evening and almost night when we drove up there. It took all day to drive there. It was toward evening by the time we got there and set up camp.

sentence.sent_text: Miish azhigwa ani-onaagoshig bagamidaabii'iweyaang, mii azhigwa gegaa dibikak.
Mii azhigwa ani-onaagoshig azhigwa ezhi-ayaayaang, ezhi-onakidooyaang.

paragraph.text_eng: I had a kitten. I wouldn't leave it behind. The kitten was small so I held it. They set up camp and cooked. They had tents. As they finished putting them up, I was holding my kitten. I was afraid it would go some place. I heard all sorts of things. Listening to the hooting of the owls, I was afraid that one would catch it.

sentence.sent_text: Miish i'iw onakidoowaad i'iw ayi'ii, jiibaakwewaad.
Giizhakidoowaad iniw bagiwayaanegamigoon ezhi-dakonag a'aw ingaazhagensim.
Gookooko'oog nwaandaagoziwaad bizindawagwaa, ingosaa gookooko'oo ji-debibinaad.

paragraph.text_eng: It was cool so I was sitting by the fire getting warm and holding my kitten. It was scared. It was afraid of the fire, maybe from seeing the flames. It __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ got scared and slipped away from me, and when it jumped in the fire, they grabbed it, as I was bawling, and put out the fire on it. My kitten was kind of singed but didn't die.

sentence.sent_text: Namadabiyaan gaye niin jiigishkode awazoyaan daki-ayaamagad, awazoyaan dakonag ingaazhagensim.
Ogii-kotaan i'iw ishkode ganabaj gichi-boodawaadenig __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ ganawaabandang.
Gaa-izhi-zegizid, miish gaa-izhi-bishigonag, gaa-izhi-gwaashkwanid imaa ishkodeng, nawadinaawaad gichi-mawiyaan, nawadinaawaad, aatebinaawaad.

paragraph.text_eng: Early in the morning they got ready and packed pails for berry-picking. I chased after them, crying, wanting to play.

sentence.sent_text: Miish i'iw gegizhebaawagak azhigwa ayaawaad, obimoomaawaan igaye akikoon, mawinzowaad.

paragraph.text_eng: Toward evening, they had a lot of berries, so they harnessed up. One of them harnessed up and then they left us. The old lady and a woman started off for Brainerd, driving there to sell the blueberries.

sentence.sent_text: Mii azhigwa ani-onaagoshig, azhigwa niibowa ayaamowaad iniw miinan, mii ezhi-onapijigewaad.
Bezhig igo onapijige, miish niinawind ezhi-naganigooyaang.
Miish a'aw mindimooyenh miinawaa bezhig a'aw ikwe ezhi-maajaawaad Oshki-oodenaang iwidi izhidaabii'iwewaad o-adaawaagewaad iniw miinan.

paragraph.text_eng: That's the way they made their living, selling berries and buying lard, flour, sugar, whatever they needed. That's the only way the Indians made their living long ago, always working on their own. After we got through picking berries, we went home and the garden was almost ready then. Everything was ripe, and we picked all sorts of things.

sentence.sent_text: Mii akeyaa gaa-onji-bimaadiziwaad adaawaagewaad iniw miinan, adaawewaad bimide miinawaa bakwezhiganan miinawaa ziinzibaakwad waa-aabajitoowaad igo.
Mii eta akeyaa gaa-izhi-bimaadiziwaad mewinzha ingiw anishinaabeg, gii-anokiitaazowaad.
Ishkwaa-mawinzoyaang, bi-giiweyaang, mii azhigwa giizhiging gegaa i'iw gitigaan.
Akina gego atitemagak, ezhi-mawinzoyaan anooj igo gegoo.

paragraph.text_eng: That's the way we used to live long ago. That's it.

Long ago we lived at Portage Lake. One of my aunts said, "Let's go to the store." I wanted to go along. I wanted to go with her to the store. The storekeeper, Waandane he was called, used to give me candy.

sentence.sent_text: Miish a'aw ninoshenh, bezhig wa'aw ninoshenh, "Adaawewigamigong izhaadaa," ikido.
Ziinzibaakwadoons iko nimiinig a'aw Waandane gii-inaa a'aw adaawewinini.

paragraph.text_eng: I was determined to go along, so I went with her. We went a long way, maybe five or six miles.

sentence.sent_text: Waasa ingii-izhaamin ingoji go naanan maagizhaa gaye ingodwaaswi diba'igan.

paragraph.text_eng: And then I remember again that we were walking along in the road, the wagon road. It was only as big as a wagon. I was barefoot and kicked the stones as we walked along.

sentence.sent_text: Miish eta go miinawaa imaa gezikwendamaan imaa ini-bimoseyaang miikana, odaabaanikana.
Mii eta go eniginid a'aw odaabaan.
Inzhaashaaginizide gaye, basikawaanagwaa ingiw asiniinsag imaa ani-bimoseyaan.

paragraph.text_eng: All of a sudden there was a real small turtle crawling along. When I looked there, there were a lot of turtles crawling around. They had just hatched.

sentence.sent_text: Baanimaa go imaa gaa-bimooded mikinaakoons enda-agaashiinyi.
Mii imaa izhi-inaabiyaan indigo naa gaa-wanoodewaad mikinaakoonsag.

paragraph.text_eng: "Hurry up," she said turning to look at me, "so we get home before evening."
"No," I told her, "I won't leave these little turtles. I wonder where they are going."
She was just mad. "Wrap them in your skirt! Pick them up! We'll go by a lake on our way," she said.
And so I got busy and picked them up while she waited for me, picked up about thirty, a __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ whole lot of those turtles, and wrapped them in my little skirt as we walked along.

sentence.sent_text: Mii imaa endazhitaayaan maamiginagwaa baabii'id imaa, maamiginagwaa ingoji go nisimidana, niibowa sa go __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ mikinaakoonsag, imaa ingoodaazhenzhishing ezhi-wiiweginagwaa, bimoseyaang.

paragraph.text_eng: Sure enough after a while there was a lake. "Go and put those turtles in," she said. As we went by the shore, I released them one-by-one in the water.

sentence.sent_text: Gomaapii dash igo azhigwa geget zaaga'igan imaa ayaamagad.

paragraph.text_eng: "I'm afraid they'll drown."
"No," she said, "that's where snapping turtles live," she said. And so I put them down one-by-one and watched them swim away. They were so cute.

sentence.sent_text: "Gaawiin," ikido, "mii imaa endazhiikewaad ingiw mikinaakwag," ikido.

paragraph.text_eng: And that's all I remember of that.

sentence.sent_text: Mii eta go imaa minik gezikwendamaan.

paragraph.text_eng: When we lived there at Portage Lake, my uncle used to look for the horses. We had horses.

sentence.sent_text: Iwidi ko gaa-taayaang Gabekanaansing, miish a'aw inzhishenh nandawasimwed iko.

paragraph.text_eng: Once there was a great thunderstorm in the night and in the morning -- I wondered where he was going -- he went looking for the horses. The horses used to have a bell. sentence.sent_text: Miish ingoding gaa-izhi-gichi-animikiikaag niibaa-dibik, gegizhebaawagadinig -- dibi iidog waa-izhaagwen -- gaa-izhi-nandawasimwed, nandawaabamaad bebezhigooganzhiin.
Agaaming giiwenh iwidi gii-debwewesinini i'iw godotaagan, gaa-izhi-maajaad iidog naanaad iniw bebezhigooganzhiin, ani-babimosed jiigibiig.

paragraph.text_eng: As he walked along the shore of one lake, he wondered about how the grass and the twigs got all broken up; he was really puzzled about what had been going on.

paragraph.text_eng: So he followed the trail. Whatever sort of thing it was, it must have crossed there at the portage and was as wide as the trail. That's how wide its track was. sentence.sent_text: Miish miinawaa imaa gaa-izhi-gakiiwenigwen, awegwenan dinowa, ingoji go enigokwadeyaag i'iw miikana.

paragraph.text_eng: The horses were scared to cross where the trail had been left by the thing that crossed. It took him a long time to lead the horses to cross.

sentence.sent_text: Mii sa giiwenh ingiw bebezhigooganzhiig gaa-izhi-gotamowaad wii-aazhogewaad imaa wii-aazhooshkaawaad imaa bimikawenid iniw gaa-aazhogenijin.
Wiikaa giiwenh ogii-kashki'aan gii-aazhogewinaad iniw bebezhigooganzhiin.

paragraph.text_eng: That's all he told about that.

I remember that long ago there used to be a great big logging camp on the other side of Mille Lacs Lake, I don't know how far. That's where all the Indians were working. The Indians who were able to went to work there. We were still living over there at Portage Lake, so my uncle came over here from there. They were having a dance up at the point. Maybe he belonged in there as a member, I don't know.

sentence.sent_text: Mewinzha gaye ingikendaan igo gichi-giishka'aakwewigamig iko gii-tagon iwidi Misi-zaaga'iganiing agaaming, amanj igo iwidi apii.

sentence.sent_text: Mii azhigwa eni-onaagoshig, azhigwa enda-zegizi nookomisiban.

paragraph.text_eng: After a while, it suddenly calmed down. We had a dock. Then she stuck her head out. "The __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ wind has gone by," she said, so we went outside and just a little ways home to sleep.

paragraph.text_eng: The next day my uncle came. He was telling us, "There was a really big storm," he said, "over there on the point. "All of the boards blew away," he said, that man told, "all of the boards blew away." I don't know how many buildings were blown down. That guy looked to see how far the cloud was and to see what was happening, and he stuck his head out of his little tent. That's when he saw a big bird there, flying toward them. It must have been the one called Wese'an 'Tornado'.

Miish iidog gaa-izhi-bazhizikaagowaad mii gaa-izhi-ombaangeninid imaa ayaawaad."

chapter.eng_title: When We Went and Weeded a Garden

paragraph.text_eng: Long ago the old lady, she wasn't so very old, raised me. There used to be a person there at Bay Lake. We called her Adaawewininiikwe, 'lady storekeeper'. It must be five, maybe three miles away from our place to where she had a store, and she wanted one of the women to go weed her garden for her. The storekeeper was an old lady. She was sick, real sick.

sentence.sent_text: Mewinzha gaye, mewinzha go, gaawiin igo aapiji gichi-mindimooyenyiwisiin iidog a'aw mindimooyenh, gaa-nitaawigi'id.
Gaa-izhi-ayaad bezhig-sh iko iwidi, Zezabegamaag gii-ayaa.

Ingoji go naano-diba'igan, maagizhaa gaye niso-diba'igan apii, imaa gaa-taayaang iwidi dash iko gii-adaawewininiikwewi a'aw; gaa-izhi-nandomaad bezhig go iniw ikwewan awiiya ji-o-bashkwashkibidaagod ogitigaan.

paragraph.text_eng: "I'll go and weed her garden, my daughter," my grandmother told the woman. "I'll go with Naawakamigookwe," she said.

sentence.sent_text: Mii dash a'aw nookomis, "Niin igo inga-o-bashkwashkibijige indaanis," odinaan iniw ikwewan.

paragraph.text_eng: Real early in the morning, she made a lunch, maybe she took bread along and a little pail -- I guess she took along the little pail because she wanted to make tea in it -- and then we left. We went straight through. We didn't follow the road. We just went right there.

sentence.sent_text: Mii sa azhigwa gegizhebaawagadinig aapiji gaa-izhi-nawapwaaniked, maagizhaa gaye bakwezhiganan gaa-maajiinaagwen miinawaa akikoonsan -- maagizhaa gaye waa-aniibiishikegwen imaa, gaa-onji-maajiinaad iniw akikoonsan, akikoon, akikoonsan igo -- gaa-izhi-maajaayaang.

paragraph.text_eng: As we walked along, we came across a little lake. That lake was small. There was a duck there, a mallard, and she picked up a stone and hit it. She killed it. She was very happy that she killed the duck, and she went and got it. It wasn't very __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ far out in the lake, but just close. Then right there she plucked the duck, built a fire, and singed it.

sentence.sent_text: Ingoding imaa ini-bimoseyaang, bezhig igo zaaga'igaans.
Zhiishiib imaa gii-paa-ayaa, ininishib; mamaad iniw asiniin, gaa-izhi-bakite'waad.
Oo, minwendam, minwendam niiwana'waad iniw zhiishiiban, ezhi-de-niiwana'waad, gaa-izhi-debibinaad.
Gaawiin __MIDPARAPAGEBREAK__ igo naawij imaa gii-ayaasiin, besho go imaa.
Miish imaa gaa-izhi-ayaad, gaa-izhi-bashkobinaad, mii iniw zhiishiiban, gaa-izhi-boodawed imaa, banzwaad.

paragraph.text_eng: "Oh, Naawakamigook, we're going to eat," the old lady, Gichi-aakogwan, said after she got through singeing it. "Oh no, we haven't even got a knife along," she said. "Look around there for a sharp stone," she told me. I couldn't spot any. I didn't know what sort of stone I was looking for. Pretty soon, she stood up, went to the shore, and started looking around right along there. Then she started noisily pounding on a stone. Then she came over. All of a sudden that stone was real sharp. That's what she used to cut up the duck which she cooked in the little pail she was carrying.

sentence.sent_text: "Oo, Naawakamigook, mii ji-wiisiniyang," ikido a'aw mindimooyenh, Gichi-aakogwan, gaa-kiizhi-banzwaad.
"Oo, yay, gaawiin sha naa gegoo mookomaan gibimiwidoosiimin," ikido.
Gaawiin ninisidawinawaasiin awenen dino asin a'aw ge-nandawaabamag.
Ingoding bazigwii, maajaad imaa babaa-ayinaabid imaa jiigibiig igo gaye go nawaj baa-ayinaabid imaa.
Azhigwa wegwaagi, mii a'aw asin enda-giinizi.
Miish iniw gaa-aabaji'aajin gii-kiishkizhwaad iniw zhiishiiban, gaa-izhi-jiibaakwaanaad imaa iniw akikoonsan bemiwinaajin.

paragraph.text_eng: Oh boy, we had a big dinner. The soup was delicious with the bread we'd packed for lunch. Then we left.

sentence.sent_text: Enda-minwaagamin igaye naboob miinawaa bakwezhigan gii-nawapoyaang; ezhi-maajaayaang.

paragraph.text_eng: The garden she went to weed was small. Well, I helped her a little there, and then when it was getting to be evening she finished, went into the store, and said that we had finished the garden. The lady storekeeper paid her and she bought what we needed. The storekeeper fed me things like cookies and candy, and we started off again. It was getting late in the evening when we came home.

sentence.sent_text: Aanish naa niwiidookawaa gaye niin bangii go imaa; azhigwa onaagoshig gaye gaa-izhi-giizhiitaad, imaa adaawewigamigong biindiged, dibaajimod, dibaajimoyaang gii-kiizhiikamaang gitigaan.
